analysis.evidence: הָבָה נִבְנֶה לָּנוּ עִיר (“Come, let us build ourselves a city”) gives the speakers’ own words.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural.

draft.change: Add the exhortative sense come-now to the Hebrew Qal of יָהַב.
draft.definition: The imperative הָבָה introduces a proposal and urges the hearer to act with the speaker.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 11:3, הָבָה introduces נִלְבְּנָה, “let us make bricks,” followed by וְנִשְׂרְפָה, “and let us burn them.” Both cohortatives express the shared undertaking.

analysis.evidence: הָבָה introduces נִבְנֶה לָּנוּ עִיר וּמִגְדָּל, “let us build ourselves a city and a tower.” The first-person plural verb and לָּנוּ, “for ourselves,” show that the speakers propose a shared undertaking.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second masculine singular, with final paragogic ה. The singular form serves as a fixed exhortation addressed to the group.
analysis.sense: Urge the hearer to join the speaker in a proposed action.

analysis.evidence: הָבָה introduces a proposal, giving נִבְנֶה the force of “let us build.” The objects עִיר וּמִגְדָּל, “a city and a tower,” establish the construction sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal first-person common plural cohortative. The initial נִ־ marks the plural speaker. For this final־ה verb, the cohortative and imperfect have the same form.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:12 as evidence for the existing city sense of עִיר in article 3yr.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:12, הָעִיר הַגְּדֹלָה describes a named settlement as “the great city.”

analysis.evidence: In נִבְנֶה לָּנוּ עִיר וּמִגְדָּל, “let us build ourselves a city and a tower,” עִיר and מִגְדָּל are the two objects of “build.” The speakers propose building a settlement.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עִיר וּמִגְדָּל names the two things the speakers propose to build, “a city and a tower.” The description וְרֹאשׁוֹ בַשָּׁמַיִם (“with its top in the heavens”) identifies the tower by its height.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” מִגְדָּל is a common noun of either gender, singular and absolute. The masculine singular suffix in וְרֹאשׁוֹ (“and its top”) refers back to the tower.

analysis.evidence: The builders describe a מִגְדָּל (“tower”) with its רֹאשׁ בַשָּׁמַיִם (“top in the heavens”). This locates the tower’s highest part.
analysis.morphology: וְ means “and.” רֹאשׁ is a masculine singular noun in the construct state. The third-person masculine singular suffix וֹ means “its” and refers to the tower.

analysis.evidence: וְרֹאשׁוֹ בַשָּׁמַיִם means “with its top in the sky.” The builders describe the intended height of the tower.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ is fused with the definite article, giving בַ and doubling the following שׁ. The noun is common, masculine, dual in form, and in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם is the object and לָּנוּ identifies the beneficiaries. The speakers propose to “make a name for ourselves,” that is, to establish a reputation by building the city and tower.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins a Qal first-person common plural verb to נִבְנֶה. With this final־ה verb, the form can also be read as an imperfect, but the exhortation הָבָה supports the cohortative reading.

analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
